subject: Reserved capacity: Helio AI coverage and pricing cushion request
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helio: request for cushion on reserved-term pricing

Hi Kim / Karthik —

Julia from Helio reached out with a last-minute ask: they want an explicit "coverage cushion" in the reserved capacity commitment that limits price exposure if spot GPU prices spike beyond a defined threshold. Their procurement team is asking for a partial rebate / credit if we cannot maintain the originally quoted per-GPU effective rate due to market movement. They framed it as a risk-sharing clause tied to our GPU procurement costs.

Attached is the latest proposal from Helio (helio_proposal_v2.pdf). High level: they are signing for 120 reserved GPU-months across Q3–Q4 2026 with a 24-month commit. They want a floor protection that would reduce their unit price by up to 15% if our realized fleet costs go above the index in the doc, and conversely, they expect us to pass through some savings if costs drop.

 asks:
- Can we give them a limited coverage window (e.g., first 6 months) where we offer a modest credit?
- If so, what guardrails (caps, look-back windows, triggers) do we need so Finance is comfortable?

Karthik — can you run the sensitivity scenarios (short delta / long delta) and add a recommended approval path for a discount band (0–10% / 10–15%) and any required exec sign-offs?
Kim — I expect Procurement will want to see a clear fallback (swap to Dedicated Lite, reduced throughput) if we hit capacity constraints. Looping Marissa since this may need a one-off authorization.

Thanks,
David

--
David Kim
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helio: request for cushion on reserved-term pricing

David

I ran three sensitivity buckets in the attached spreadsheet (sensitivity_model.xlsx):
1) Base case: fleet cost delta +/- 8% annualized (our expectation based on current forward offers)
2) Shock case: one-time spike that increases realized fleet cost by 22% over a 3-month window
3) Prolonged inflation: sustained +12% for 9 months then normalizes

My recommendation: offer a 6-month coverage window with a cap on credits at 5% of the committed revenue for the first year. Triggers are measured against our internal GPU inventory cost index (weekly avg). Look-back to the last 4 weeks to determine trigger. If realized index exceeds the threshold by >12% in any 4-week period, Helio would receive a one-time credit equal to (realized-index premium * committed-unit-rate) up to the 5% cap.

Approval path suggested:
- Up to 3% credit: Sales head sign-off (David) + Revenue Ops (Marissa)
- 33%: EVP Sales (Kimberly) + Finance (FP&A director)
- >10%: requires CFO + Legal + CEO notification

I've included an illustrative P&L impact table in the sheet. Note: this assumes we can keep the reserved pool elastic (burst into spot) -- if not, downside increases materially.

-Karthik
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helio: request for cushion on reserved-term pricing

Team,

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of operational constraints we need to call out for Procurement:
- We cannot publicly commit to pass-through discounts tied to third-party vendor listed prices; any index must be agreed and auditable. Propose our internal index (weekly spot burn + committed procurement contracts) with audit rights for Helio under NDA only.
- Any credit mechanism must be symmetrical in accounting (credits booked as contra-revenue) and capped at the percentage Karthik suggested. Finance will require quarterly reconciliation and a contingency reserve on the balance sheet for expected worst-case credits.

Marissa 3 can you confirm if we have precedent for a 5% cap and what the accounting tags would be? Also need Legal to draft limited audit rights language (NDA addendum) and a fallback clause that allows us to re-tier Helio to a lower throughput SLA if we hit a sustained supply shortage.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
VP, Revenue Operations
From: Julia Park <julia@helio.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: Helio AI coverage and pricing cushion request

David/Kim/Karthik 3 thanks for the fast analysis and proposed structure. A few clarifications from Procurement:
- Helio is comfortable with an internal index as long as its transparent and we get quarterly visibility (no full vendor audit; summary metrics suffice).
- We'd like the coverage window extended to 9 months if the credit cap stays at or below 7%.
- If the trigger is a 12% deviation, we want the calculation to use a 6-week look-back rather than 4 weeks to avoid false positives from single-week spikes.

Can you send a redline of the terms with the numeric buckets and fallback options? We can aim to close this next week.

Best,
Julia Park
VP Procurement, Helio AI
